mathematical_comparison: All three public types match the authored source. The zero-tail sum proof is valid in an additive commutative monoid. In the wide case, ordered orthonormal completion gives later-coordinate zeros without independence assumptions; full basis expansion, prefix restriction and coordinate evaluation give A=RQ, while the row Gram matrix gives QQ^T=I. In the tall case R=A,Q=I_n is valid. Empty, zero, deficient-rank and square cases introduce no missing premise. No mathematical mismatch or repair was found.

semantic_slots.target: Exact real A=RQ with R:m-by-r,Q:r-by-n,r=min(m,n) and QQ^T=I_r matches both source and Lean. Width is not rank(A); no triangularity, uniqueness or canonical factor selection is claimed.
semantic_slots.normalization: Existing Q rows have real dot products delta_kl, hence unit norms and pairwise orthogonality. No normalization of A or R is assumed. State-vector normalization and block-encoding scaling are not applicable to this finite-matrix existence theorem.
semantic_slots.registers: No quantum registers are present. Fin indices specify row-first matrix coordinates and exact factor dimensions; ordinary transpose swaps indices. Qubit/tensor ordering and endianness are not applicable and are not implicitly introduced.
semantic_slots.oracles: No oracle or access model is assumed. Mathlib completion, basis expansion and finite sum results are internal proof dependencies, not quantum or classical black-box input oracles.
semantic_slots.ancillas_phases: No circuit ancilla, workspace, garbage or phase contract is present. Scalars are real and transpose is ordinary transpose. Noncanonical orthonormal-completion witnesses do not imply a circuit phase or cleanup theorem.
semantic_slots.error_success: Both equations are exact for all allowed inputs, including zero and empty shapes. There are no tolerances, numerical stability assertions, random success guarantees or postselection sectors.
semantic_slots.resources: Only factor shapes are asserted. Choice-based existence does not provide stored factors, deterministic numerical extraction, runtime, query/gate counts or finite-bit synthesis. The source explicitly declines these claims and no such clause appears in the public theorem types.
